tasks.title: Finalize thick-owner-thinning OpenSpec artifacts
tasks.description: Keep the OpenSpec change as the source-of-truth contract for thinning `OpenCodianView.ts` and `OpenCodeService.ts` without fragmenting files.
tasks.details: Review and refine `openspec/changes/thick-owner-thinning/proposal.md`, `design.md`, `specs/high-connection-owner-thinning/spec.md`, and `tasks.md` so they all encode the same rules: alternating service/view lanes, exactly one stable ownership slice per round, preference for existing adjacent owners, and full guardrail verification. The output of this task is a valid OpenSpec change that Task Master and `opencode-loop` can consume.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `openspec validate thick-owner-thinning` and `openspec status --change thick-owner-thinning` to confirm the change is valid and all artifacts are complete.

tasks.title: Initialize Task Master for the thick-owner-thinning change
tasks.description: Configure Task Master to parse the OpenSpec proposal using a provider that is actually available in this environment.
tasks.details: Keep `.taskmaster/config.json` aligned with the available DeepSeek-compatible setup, then parse `openspec/changes/thick-owner-thinning/proposal.md` into `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json`. The resulting tasks must stay centered on the OpenSpec contract rather than inventing unrelated automation layers.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `task-master parse-prd openspec/changes/thick-owner-thinning/proposal.md --num-tasks 8` with the required OpenAI-compatible environment variable bridge and confirm `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` is generated.

tasks.title: Normalize Task Master tasks to the real refactor lanes
tasks.description: Replace any Task Master output that invents unrelated scripts or templates with tasks that match the actual maintainability program.
tasks.details: Edit `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` so the queue aligns with the OpenSpec tasks: pipeline setup, queue enrichment, alternating service/view lanes, and execute-mode hardening. Every task must map to a real repo action and avoid introducing speculative helper scripts, fake templates, or behavior not requested by the OpenSpec change.
tasks.testStrategy: Review `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` and confirm every task maps back to `openspec/changes/thick-owner-thinning/tasks.md` and the anti-fragmentation contract.

tasks.title: Import Task Master tasks into opencode-loop execute mode
tasks.description: Create `.opencode-loop/queue.json` from the normalized Task Master task list instead of continuing to rely on the broad `dev` loop program.
tasks.details: Use `opencode-loop plan --dir /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian --from-taskmaster --tag master` to import `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` into execute mode. Ensure the import does not overwrite unrelated state unexpectedly and that the resulting queue starts with tasks in draft status.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `opencode-loop plan --dir /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian --from-taskmaster --tag master`, then verify `.opencode-loop/queue.json` exists and contains imported draft tasks.

tasks.title: Enrich queue tasks with repo-specific verification and acceptance checks
tasks.description: Add the concrete gate contract each execute-mode task must satisfy in this repo.
tasks.details: Update `.opencode-loop/queue.json` so each task carries appropriate `verification` commands and `acceptance_checks`. The checks must encode the real contract for this program: single-slice ownership movement, updated module docs, graphify freshness when `src/` changes, and `npm run verify`. Use focused checks for setup tasks and full verify for refactor tasks.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `opencode-loop queue validate --dir /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian` and inspect the enriched queue entries to confirm verification and acceptance fields are present.

tasks.title: Finalize execute-mode readiness
tasks.description: Record that the execute queue is ready and the repo has been initialized for execute-mode runs.
tasks.details: Complete the local bootstrap so `opencode-loop` can run in `execute` mode against the imported queue. This includes validating the queue, initializing execute mode for the repo, and making sure the next code-bearing task can start from a clean, resumable baseline.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `opencode-loop init --dir /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian --mode execute`, then confirm `opencode-loop status --dir /Volumes/SDD2T/obsidian-vault-write/custom-project/opencodian --json` reports execute-mode runtime settings.

tasks.title: Thin OpenCodeService request and transport ownership
tasks.description: Move one low-risk `OpenCodeService.ts` behavior slice into existing adjacent owners without creating helper-file fragments.
tasks.details: Target a single stable `OpenCodeService.ts` slice, preferably request assembly or transport/config ownership that already borders existing owners such as `OpenCodePromptRequestBuilder`, `OpenCodeCatalogQueryCoordinator`, or `OpenCodeServiceLifecycleCoordinator`. The task must explicitly avoid multi-slice refactors and thin helper proliferation.
tasks.testStrategy: Run focused OpenCodeService unit tests, refresh graphify if `src/` changes, and finish with `npm run verify`. Review the diff to confirm exactly one service-lane slice moved.

tasks.title: Thin OpenCodianView message rendering ownership
tasks.description: Move one low-risk `OpenCodianView.ts` message-rendering slice into existing adjacent owners without fragmenting the chat runtime.
tasks.details: After the first service-lane round lands, target one stable `OpenCodianView.ts` message-rendering slice that already touches adjacent owners such as existing renderers, runtime bridges, or user-message helpers. Keep the work to one slice, preserve per-tab behavior, and avoid creating a spray of tiny helper files.
tasks.testStrategy: Run focused chat rendering tests, refresh graphify if `src/` changes, and finish with `npm run verify`. Review the diff to confirm exactly one view-lane slice moved.
